overview.text: The Southern African Rock Python is one of the largest snakes in the world. It is non-venomous and kills prey by squeezing.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 2.8 to 4 m; over 4.6 m is rare. Females are much bigger than males.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern Africa: from Angola, Zambia, Tanzania and Kenya south to South Africa.

diet.text: Mainly small antelopes, jackals, hares and monkeys, occasionally fish and even crocodiles.

reproduction.text: Lays 30 to 60 eggs, sometimes over 100. The mother guards and warms them and may stay with the young for two weeks or more after hatching.

funfacts.text: Mother rock pythons may stay with their babies for weeks after they hatch - unusual for a snake.

recognise.text: Huge, heavy python with a blotched pattern.
